quote: Till rising and gliding out I wander’d off by myself, / In the mystical moist night-air, and from time to time, / Look’d up in perfect silence at the stars.
source: Walt Whitman, When I Heard the Learn’d Astronomer, the closing three lines, Leaves of Grass, Book XX, By the Roadside

evidence.where: the Project Gutenberg text of Leaves of Grass, downloaded and read this run; the poem stands at line 8906 of that file and the nearest preceding cluster heading is BOOK XX. BY THE ROADSIDE
evidence.edition: Leaves of Grass, the 1891 to 1892 deathbed edition, which prints the elisions wander’d and Look’d
evidence.locator: the last three of the poem’s eight lines, Book XX, By the Roadside

reason: The three lines match the scanned text exactly, including both elided spellings, the hyphen in night-air and the comma after from time to time. The poem first appeared in Drum-Taps in 1865. Whitman has no other line in the year.
